subject: [AMBER] Amber18 compiled with GCC/8.3.0 fails some DPFP tests

messages.author: Cong Liu
messages.body:
Dear Amber Developers,
I recently compiled Amebr18 with GCC/8.3.0 and CUDA/10.1. The compilation
went through well. However, *amber_cuda_serial *testing indicates 5 "*file
comparison failure*":  DPFP myoglobin_igb7, DPFP myoglobin_igb8, DPFP
myoglobin_igb8_gbsa, DPFP irest1_ntt0_igb7_ntc2, DPFP irest1_ntt0_igb8_ntc2
with "IEEE_UNDERFLOW_FLAG IEEE_DENORMAL" floating-point exceptions.
The compile parameters:
1.  ./configure gnu;
2. make install;
Can I ignore this error or I should compile Amber again with different
settings?
Best,
Cong Liu

>with "IEEE_UNDERFLOW_FLAG IEEE_DENORMAL" floating-point exceptions.
The underflow flag is not worrisome, but you should look at the .dif
files (collected in the logs folder) and see if the discrepancies look
like roundoff errors or something more serious.
....dac

messages.author: Kellon Belfon
messages.body:
Hi Cong,
The Etot difference is because of the EGB difference.
What kind of GPUs are these? Are the GPUs the volta architecture e.g V100?
I know there were some issues with racemic conditions on the volta
architecture and register spillage from one of my GPU kernels (though this
kernel is in amber20 and not in amber18) for the GB calculations on the
GPU.
Dave Cerutti knows more about this since he was been working on it/worked
on it. I know this was happening in newer version of Amber but I think it
is maybe the same issue in Amber 18 if it is one of the newer GPUs.
Regards,
Kellon
